🧠 Crypto News Brief: Markets turned risk-off as Iran strikes and rising Fed rate-hike odds pushed Bitcoin below $78K, yet steady ETF inflows and expanding institutional infrastructure show underlying demand hasn't cracked. 📉 Iran Strikes Trigger Broad Crypto Selloff, Bitcoin Slips to $77.5K Bitcoin, XRP, Solana and other major tokens sold off in tandem after U.S. airstrikes on Iran sent oil above $90 a barrel and bond yields higher. High-beta tokens like Solana and Tron fell over 3% while Bitcoin slipped roughly 1% to around $77,500, as traders priced in the risk of tighter Fed policy. Read full story 🏦 Fed Rate Hike Odds Climb to 68% as Oil Spike Muddies Policy Outlook Crude oil's jump past $90 a barrel pushed the market-implied odds of a September 16 Fed rate hike to 68%, dragging bitcoin, gold and stocks lower together. Economists including Mark Zandi argue a hike would be a policy error, since an oil-driven supply shock isn't the inflation rate hikes are meant to fix. More details 💧 XRP ETFs Rack Up $170M in 11-Day Inflow Streak, Goldman Leads Holders U.S. spot XRP ETFs pulled in about $170 million over 11 straight trading sessions since August 18, pushing cumulative inflows since their November launch to $1.68 billion. Q2 filings show Goldman Sachs as the largest institutional holder at roughly $87.4 million, ahead of Jane Street and Millennium Management. Read more 📊 Bitcoin ETFs Post Best Month of 2026, Then Stumble Into September Outflows Spot Bitcoin ETFs logged their strongest month of 2026 in August with $3.52 billion in net inflows as BTC rallied about 25%, lifting total fund assets to $99.61 billion. That momentum reversed fast: the funds saw $236 million in net outflows on September 1, with BlackRock's IBIT alone responsible for over $201 million of the exodus. See details ⚠️ Sui DeFi Protocol Full Sail Shuts Down After $91K Oracle Exploit Full Sail, a DeFi protocol built on Sui, is winding down after an attacker drained roughly $91,000 from three vaults by exploiting its Switchboard oracle integration. The team has halted new deposits, moved to withdrawal-only mode, and pledged to make affected users whole using remaining liquidity and team funds. Read full story 🛡️ Feds and CrowdStrike Dismantle Botnet Behind Years of Crypto-Draining Malware U.S. authorities worked with CrowdStrike and partners in Bulgaria, Hungary and Romani

Crypto Biz Newsletter

Автор: Cointelegraph


Автор: Cointelegraph

Прочитати на LinkedIn

Crypto’s August rally put corporate conviction to the test. Bitcoin (BTC) miners that spent much of the crypto downturn courting AI investors are once again trading like leveraged bets on BTC, while Strategy and Strive are adding thousands more Bitcoin to their balance sheets.  The same concentration is playing out elsewhere. Bitmine is closing in on owning 5% of  Ether’s (ETH) circulating supply despite billions in unrealized losses, while 21 major financial institutions are taking a different approach by developing stablecoins for payments and settlement. Bitcoin rally puts miners back in the spotlight Bitcoin’s August rally lifted beaten-down mining stocks by as much as 67%, reversing a trend that had favored miners pivoting to AI and underscoring the sector’s continued sensitivity to BTC market conditions. BlocksBridge Consulting reported in a recent newsletter that Bitcoin’s roughly 23% rally in late August outpaced most AI-linked infrastructure stocks. Canaan, American Bitcoin and Cango gained between 41% and 67%, compared with about 21% for CoreWeave, 17% for Nebius and 15% for IREN. Meanwhile, some miners with greater exposure to AI and high-performance computing were flat or declined. BlocksBridge cited three catalysts for the rally: an expansion of US Treasury liquidity-supporting buybacks, renewed regulatory optimism following a White House crypto meeting and a sharp short squeeze that liquidated more than $1.6 billion in positions. The outperformance suggests investors may once again be rewarding direct Bitcoin exposure, although the sector still faces risks from the high costs of building out AI data-center capacity. Continue Reading… Strive, Strategy add to Bitcoin holdings as BTC rallies Strive and Strategy added billions of dollars’ worth of Bitcoin to their corporate treasuries in the final week of August, with Strive buying 1,800 BTC for approximately $143 million and Strategy acquiring another 4,603 BTC. Strive’s purchases between Aug. 24 and Aug. 28 lifted its holdings to 23,156 BTC, making it the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder. The company paid an average of $79,431 per BTC, including fees and expenses, after buying 1,110 BTC the prior week at an average price of $73,409.
